patients.label: 22-year-old girl with heartbreak, hopelessness, depression and suicidal ideation treated with single-session rapid tele-psychotherapy with music therapy

identity_evidence.quote: I report the case of a 22-year-old broken-hearted girl with hopelessness, depression, and suicidal ideation.

attribution_limitations: The appendix says validated scales or measures were used for depression, hopelessness and suicidal ideation, while the limitations and discussion say standardized and validated instruments were not applied and the 0-10 scaling questions are not standardized psychometric instruments.

The case report says she composed the new lyrics (the “soundtrack of my life”) in the closing stages, whereas the discussion places the lyric creation in the working stage and calls the soundtrack created on the previous working stage.

The text says the patient/client explained the procedures to be carried out during the RTP-SSMT at the transition stage; the wording does not make clear whether the patient or the therapist explained them.
The discussion calls the outcome measure “suicidal intent” once and “suicidal ideation” elsewhere for the same self-rated scale.

The author interprets the course (logotherapy meaning-making, music-based reframing, a "talking cure", predicted further score decrease, probable influence of work and church) as claims or hypotheses; these are not recorded as patient facts.

The sentence on increased participation in meaningful social and spiritual activities sits in the working-stage paragraph but does not say whether the participation happened during the session or afterwards.

She had previously received counseling from colleagues, with some but not full relief. She was described as a nonvoluntarily-referred patient.
